# The Morning Break — A Surfing Pelican

An animated, **non-interactive** Three.js diorama: a white pelican with a
long orange beak and wobbling pouch carves an endless golden-hour wave on a
coral surfboard. There are no controls to learn — open the page and watch.

## What's in the scene

- **Procedural pelican** — plump body, S-curved neck, crested head turned
  into the ride, flattened beak with hooked tip and pouch, black-tipped
  wings spread for balance, webbed feet, and a board leash.
- **Endless ride** — she pumps up and down the wave face, traverses along
  it, crouches to absorb each turn, counter-balances with her wings, and
  pops a small hop roughly every twelve seconds.
- **Curling hero wave** — a bent-plane wave face with a translucent barrel,
  pulsing foam lip, churning whitewater, falling lip mist, and spray kicked
  up behind the board.
- **Golden-hour world** — gradient sky dome, low sun, animated ocean swells,
  drifting clouds, and flapping distant seabirds.
- **Cinematic camera** — a slow drift that keeps the rider framed. The page
  is deliberately non-interactive: no mouse, touch, or keyboard controls.
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` by calming the animation.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | Entry point; loads `style.css` and `main.js` |
| `main.js` | All Three.js scene, model-building, and animation code |
| `style.css` | Page layout, caption card, and vignette |
| `package.json` | Declares the `three` dependency |

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm run check   # verify the bundle: esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm
```

The page imports `three` by package name and is packaged afterwards into a
single self-contained `index.html` with esbuild, so it runs fully offline
with no network requests and no browser storage.

Done — the surfing pelican is built and verified, ready for packaging into a single self-contained page afterwards.

**What you get:** "The Morning Break," a non-interactive Three.js diorama in which a procedural white pelican — S-curved neck, long orange beak with a wobbling pouch, black-tipped wings spread for balance, and webbed feet on a coral surfboard — carves an endless golden-hour wave. She pumps up and down the curling wave face (sampled directly from the wave's own profile so the board truly rides the surface), traverses along it, crouches into each turn, and pops a small hop every twelve seconds, with spray, lip mist, foam, animated ocean swells, drifting clouds, distant seabirds, and a slow cinematic camera drift. There are no controls at all, and `prefers-reduced-motion` calms the animation.

**Files:** [index.html](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-wonder-full-1.0-mc-xhigh-20261017-090728/work/index.html) loads [main.js](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-wonder-full-1.0-mc-xhigh-20261017-090728/work/main.js) and [style.css](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-wonder-full-1.0-mc-xhigh-20261017-090728/work/style.css), with `three` installed via npm and a short [README.md](<vol>/dev/art-crit-runs/2026-10-17-090728-surfing-pelican/muse-wonder-full-1.0-mc-xhigh-20261017-090728/work/README.md).
